gdpr.note: Whichever is higher, for the most serious infringements.

ccpa.note: For intentional violations or those involving minors under 16. Others are up to $2,663. Both rise with inflation.

lgpd.value: 2% of Brazil revenue, up to R$50M

pipl.note: For serious violations, plus possible suspension.

ukgdpr.note: Whichever is higher, for the most serious infringements.

fadp.note: A criminal fine on responsible individuals for intentional breaches. A business can be fined up to CHF 50,000 in some cases.

pdpa-ar.note: Stacked fines are capped at ARS 50 million. Serious cases can also suspend or close a database.

lpdp-uy.note: Fines in indexed units (UI), capped by law. Sanctions run from observation to closure.

pipa-kr.note: Normally up to 3%. Up to 10% for repeated, very large or defiant violations since September 2026.

appi.note: A criminal fine on corporations that defy a PPC order or misuse a database. Surcharges arrive with the 2026 amendment.

nzpa.note: A fine for specific offences; no GDPR-scale administrative fines.

popia.note: An administrative fine. Serious offences can also bring a fine, up to ten years in prison, or both.

kdpa.value: Up to KES 5M or 1% of turnover
kdpa.note: Whichever is lower, for the most serious cases.

dpdp.note: Imposed by the Data Protection Board, from 13 May 2027.

gdpr.note: One-stop-shop for cross-border cases. The EDPB settles disputes between authorities.

ccpa.note: CalPrivacy, formally the California Privacy Protection Agency, is a dedicated privacy regulator.

lgpd.note: A national regulatory agency since 2026. Its first large fine came in August 2026.

pipl.note: The CAC leads, with sector-specific oversight.

ukgdpr.note: Replaced the Information Commissioner on 30 September 2026.

fadp.note: The Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner investigates and orders. Cantonal authorities impose fines.

pdpa-ar.note: The Agency for Access to Public Information.

lpdp-uy.note: The Personal Data Regulation and Control Unit.

appi.note: The Personal Information Protection Commission of Japan.

nzpa.note: Issues compliance notices and enforceable decisions.

kdpa.note: The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner.

dpdp.note: Set up in 2025, with members still to be appointed as of August 2026. Its powers start 13 May 2027.

ccpa.note: Data-breach claims only. Damages run $107 to $799 per consumer per incident, or actual damages if higher.

pipl.note: With a reversed burden of proof on handlers.

ukgdpr.note: Compensation for damage, mirroring the EU GDPR.

fadp.note: Civil claims for breach of personality under the Civil Code.

pdpa-ar.note: The habeas data action lets individuals sue directly.

lpdp-uy.note: The habeas data action is available to individuals.

pipa-kr.note: Damages with the burden on the company, up to five times for intentional leaks, or fixed statutory damages.

appi.note: Court claims for disclosure, correction or cessation after a prior demand, plus general tort claims.

nzpa.note: Complaints escalate to the Human Rights Review Tribunal for damages.

popia.note: Civil action for damages, without needing to prove fault.

dpdp.note: No private right of action. The Board will handle complaints from 13 May 2027.

ccpa.note: Statutory amounts per violation rather than turnover tiers.

lgpd.note: Graduated sanctions from warning to fine to suspension.

pipl.note: Escalates to business suspension and personal liability.

ukgdpr.note: Two tiers, mirroring the EU GDPR.

fadp.note: Criminal fines tied to specific breaches rather than turnover tiers.

pdpa-ar.note: Graduated from warning to fine to database closure.

lpdp-uy.note: Graduated from observation to fine to suspension.

pipa-kr.note: Administrative surcharges plus criminal penalties by severity.

appi.note: Escalates from guidance to order to penalty for defying an order.

nzpa.note: Compliance notices and tribunal orders rather than turnover tiers.

popia.note: Enforcement notices, then an administrative fine or prosecution for offences.

kdpa.note: Penalty notices scaled to the nature of the breach.

dpdp.note: Penalties scaled by breach type, up to the statutory maximum.
